div.head: II Cn 36
div.ab: And gyf hwa mæne að on haligdome swerige, ⁊ he oferstæled weorðe, þolige þæra handa oððe healfes weres; ⁊ þæt sy gemæne hlaforde ⁊ bisceope.
And gif hwa mæne að on haligdome swerige, ⁊ he oferstaled geweorðe, þolige þara handa oððe healfes weres; ⁊ [þæt] sy gemæne hlaforde ⁊ biscope.
Si quis falsum iuramentum super sancta iurabit et conuictus inde fuerit, manum perdat uel dimidiam wéram; et hoc commune sit domino et episcopo.
Be mænan aðe. Gyf hwa mæne að on haligdome swerie ⁊ he oferstǽled weorðe, ðolie ðara hánda oððe healfes weres, ⁊ ðæt sy gemæne hlaforde ⁊ bisceope.
And gyf hwa mæne að on haligdome swerige, and he oferstæled weorðe, þolige þæra handa oððe healfes weres, and þæt sy gemæne hlaforde and bisceope.

(Vom Meineid. B) Und wenn einer falschen Eid auf die Reliquien schwört und überführt wird, verliere er die [Schwur]hand oder [sein] halbes Wergeld; und letzteres sei halb getheilt dem [Gerichts]herrn und [halb] dem Bischof.

(Of false oaths. B) And if anyone swears a false oath on relics and is convicted, let him lose the [swearing] hand or half [his] wergild; and let the latter be shared between the lord [of the court] and the bishop.
Concerning perjury. If anyone swears a false oath on the relics and is convicted, he shall lose his hand or half his wergeld which shall be divided between the lord and the bishop.
And if anyone swears a false oath on the relics, and is confuted, he is to forfeit his hands or half his wergild; and it is to be divided by the lord and the bishop.
And if anyone swears a false oath over the relics and is convicted, he shall either lose his hand or half his wergild, which is to be shared between king and bishop.
div.note: G's ‘mæne’ for ‘mænne’. ‘þæt’ supplied in A. Liebermann compares II As 26.
B adds rubric Be mænan aðe
